Like pretty much everyone else 2026 has been the year that agentic engineering really took off at OpenAI, best illustrated by this chart: I'm intrigued at what caused that significant acceleration in AI spend per researcher in late July - my best guess is that's when internal employees gained access to the model later released as GPT-6 Astra. title: Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries (New Journal Article)
raw_text: The article linked below was published by Public Library Quarterly. Title Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries Authors Kathryn FitzGerald University of Washington Benjamin Lee University of Washington Source Public Library Quarterly DOI: 1 0.1080/01616846.2026.2725502 Abstract As artificial intelligence reshapes both library work and the information environment, public libraries must determine whether or how to engage with AI while maintaining library values. To our knowledge, there exists no published analysis of how American and Canadian public library AI policies might link library values and technology adoption. To address this gap, we conducted an environmental scan of public library websites to identify and analyze AI policy statements. Our scan of over 200 library websites identified 32 AI polcies. All reference at least two values, with privacy, security, and responsibility the most frequently cited. title: The purpose of DNS is to spread scams
raw_text: The purpose of DNS is to spread scams Terence Eden shares some daunting statistics in support of his take that "the Domain Name System's purpose seems to be a vector for criminals to run scams on people at a terrifyingly high rate". On this Interisle report ( via Andrew Campling ), Terence says: It says 85 million new registrations of gTLDs were made in 2025. Of those 8.5 million were added to blocklists by May 2025. It reckons that a 10% abuse rate is the likely floor for these numbers and it's probably closer to 20%. One in five newly registered domains with a gTLD are scams. That's a bloody crisis. I had no idea. Apparently ICANN have been discussing this problem for years. Tags: dns , scams , terence-eden

title: There's No Limit to How Bad Code Can Get
raw_text: My comment on There's No Limit to How Bad Code Can Get — Lobste.rs. [In reply to a comment about burning it down to start from scratch when technical debt becomes overwhelming] In my experience it's so rare for that to work. You announce the old thing is irrecoverably drowning in tech debt. You spin up a team to rewrite it from scratch. Work begins. Meanwhile the old thing remains a moving target: it's running the core business, so changes are still necessary. The developers working on it know that it's going to be made obsolete by the new thing soon, so they don't have any incentive to go beyond the smallest effort possible to add the new features. Technical debt continues to mount. Meanwhile, the team working on the new thing are ambitious and probably a little naive. They start out at a great pace - it's greenfield after all - but as time progresses it becomes apparent that nobody fully understands the behavior and scope of the thing they are replacing. If it was well documented and tested it wouldn't need to be replaced, after all... After months (or even years) without delivering value, the pressure is on to "ship it", so the new system is launched to handle a subset of what the old system handled - or often for some new feature that was too hard to build with the now mostly unmaintained old system. ... so now you have TWO systems in production - the janky old system that nobody wants to touch, and a new system which handles just a few production features and is 80% inac

title: Report: The Federal Program Keeping Libraries Online? the FCC Might Gut It
raw_text: From the Indianapolis Star: Under the atrium at the Indianapolis Public Library , a woman is busily typing away on her laptop. Another patron seated at the Central Branch is charging their device while streaming music through earbuds as they read quietly between the stacks. Free Wi-Fi allows Hoosiers a cozy and safe place to access the internet at all 26 library locations across Indianapolis. Potential cuts, however, by the Federal Communications Commission have put that access at risk, advocates warn, and not just in Indiana, but for millions of people in libraries and public schools across the country. The FCC recently put into question whether a 30-year-old program that helps keep libraries online should be changed, left alone, or end. No decisions have been reached, but librarians are concerned about what it could mean for their funding. In late June, the FCC issued what appeared to be a benign notice addressing child safety under one of its service operations. Buried within the 86-page document were eight words that sent shockwaves among librarians and educators alike: “Should the E-Rate program be limited or sunset?” [Clip] “This definitely caught us by surprise,” said Jamar Rahming , president-elect of the Public Library Association and CEO of Cuyahoga County Public Library in Cleveland, Ohio. “E-Rate has been just such a fixture in our public library institutions and communities.” Learn More, Read the Complete Article (about 2300 words) The post Report: The Federal Pr

raw_text: From WTOP: In 2019, Christopher Stewart started paying students in D.C. to work in a school library and learn about the field. The concept is similar to a paid internship, with students helping with research and shelving books. title: Association of American Publishers (AAP) and The Authors Guild Release New Study Analyzing the Impact of Library E-Lending on Commercial Book Markets
raw_text: From a Joint Release: Today, the Association of American Publishers (AAP) and the Authors Guild announced the release of a landmark independent study by leading economists at Secretariat Advisors, titled An Empirical Study of the Impact of Library E-Lending on the Book Economy. The study, commissioned jointly by AAP and the Authors Guild, but independently conducted by Secretariat Advisors’ economists, provides the most rigorous analysis to date of how the steep shift toward digital lending in recent years has affected the commercial marketplace for books in the United States, specifically, the consumer sales on which authors and publishers rely for financial success. The research concludes that increased digital access to e-books through library apps influences consumer behavior and impacts commercial markets across both physical and digital formats. The study further concludes there is robust and economically meaningful evidence of direct substitution between library e-lending and retail sales and that decreases in library e-book prices or certain other changes to licensing terms, as required in recent state legislative initiatives, would cause further harm to commercial markets. Authors, publishers, and libraries enjoy a close relationship and shared objective to promote and maximize reading across all levels of society, not only to champion established works of literature but to support the continued production of books not yet written. title: The Great IFLA100 Futures Challenge
raw_text: Join us on the first stage of our drive to engage the global library field in a reflection on the future(s) of our institutions, our place in society, and our international cooperation. A key pillar of the programme for IFLA’s centenary year – IFLA100 – is a focus on the future. Alongside the remembering and celebration of our past achievements and the people that made them possible, we want this year to be a chance to build up the skills, attitudes and connections necessary to enter into our second century with confidence. Central to this is our work to build up the habit of futures thinking across our profession. This enables us to steer a path between a denialism driven by passivity, and an excessive reliance on specific predictions that leaves little room to react to the unexpected. IFLA already has a strong record of work in this space. Our Trend Report in 2024 shared a set of potential trends, as well as using these to offer a range of potential scenarios for the future, ready to be used by libraries and library workers to test their own plans. Our Weak Signals report added to this, using ideas gathered at the 2025 World Library and Information Congress to identify phenomena that could potentially have a transformative effect in the future. At our 2026 Congress, the keynote speech by Sohail Inayatullah provided further insights into techniques for futures thinking, complementing the keynote given by Riel Miller at our Toronto meetings in April. title: “A Secure Environment to Explore”: Learn About the AI Sandbox Initiative For Staff at the Library of Congress
raw_text: From an LC Blog Post: In 2025, the Library introduced its AI Sandbox for staff initiative to do just that. “Sandbox” environments have been used since the early 1970s to provide protected spaces for development and experimentation without risk to systems. [Clip] While AI technologies have growing potential to augment and enrich the Library’s collections and services, experimentation and security are key. To better understand how these creative and innovative methods might work with various materials and conditions, the most recent cohort of the Library’s AI Sandbox for staff supported over a dozen small-scale experiments. Teams incorporated technical and subject matter expertise to focus their experimentation on the real-life demands and possibilities for Library workflows. [Clip] Projects focused on materials spanning the Library’s rich collections: legal records and briefs; circulars and regulations; images; talking books; audiovisual materials, classified ads from historic newspapers; web archived government PDFs; manuscript materials in Arabic, Persian, Ge’ez, Turkish, Armenian, Georgian, Japanese, Chinese, and Hebrew; children’s and young adult books, sound recordings; web archived metadata; record annotations; oral history recordings; non-Latin monographs; catalog records; training materials and resources; and even more items accessible via the Library of Congress collections API . title: Call for Proposals: Consultancy on International Association Membership, Volunteer and Congress Models
raw_text: IFLA is looking for a consultant that can support work to ensure that our membership, volunteer and Congress financial models are optimised as we enter our second century, drawing on insights and best practice from peer organisations. This work takes place as part of our Sustainable Futures Journey, which brings together a range of initiatives intended to strengthen our Federation’s ability to deliver on its current and future strategies. The work on reviews of our membership, volunteer and congress financial models is being led by members of our Governing Board, with a strong emphasis on engaging our communities and partners, and drawing on their experience and ideas. At the same time, we are realistic about the fact that there are many other international associations which face similar situations to our own, and which can offer us valuable lessons and ideas to inform our own work. This is where we are seeking a consultant who can support the work of our Board by bringing together key examples and inputs. Details of our expectations are set out in the formal call , which is open until 15 September. We welcome applications from around the world, and from teams of consultants.

title: Wouter van Balveren van OBGZ over minibiebs: “We hebben eigenlijk 350 vestigingen”
raw_text: In Nijmegen staan honderden minibiebs in de stad. De bibliotheek besloot niet te concurreren met deze kleine boekenkastjes die iedereen wel uit het straatbeeld herkent, maar juist te kijken wat ze voor elkaar kunnen betekenen. Wouter van Balveren, innovatiemanager bij OBGZ (Nijmegen en omstreken) vertelt hoe de samenwerking met de minibiebeigenaren ontstond, wat het oplevert en hoe je een samenwerking opzet. Kun je kort vertellen wat jullie met de minibiebs doen? “Minibiebs zijn natuurlijk al heel lang overal te vinden. Wij zagen ze ook om ons heen. Je kunt daar op twee manieren naar kijken. Je kunt het zien als een bedreiging en denken: dat is niet wat wij als bibliotheek zijn. Wij hebben een actuele, zorgvuldig samengestelde collectie. Wat heb je dan aan zo’n minibieb? Maar je kunt het ook anders bekijken. Het zijn enthousiaste mensen die van lezen houden en het leuk vinden om boeken en verhalen met anderen te delen. In die zin zijn het eigenlijk ambassadeurs van leesplezier, net als wij. Daarnaast past het goed bij onze missie: wij staan voor leesplezier, verhalen en toegang tot boeken voor iedereen. title: German company becomes first in Europe to launch fully commercial orbital rocket
raw_text: Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at a German university, successfully launched a privately-developed rocket into low-Earth orbit Saturday from a Norwegian spaceport inside the Arctic Circle. The two-stage rocket, named Spectrum, became the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit. With Saturday's success, Isar is the clear leader among a pack of several European launch startups vying to inject some competition into Europe's stagnant launch market. Isar's 92-foot-tall (28-meter) Spectrum rocket lifted off at 4:12 pm EST (20:12 UTC) Saturday from Andøya Spaceport in northern Norway, where it was 10:12 pm local time as the final bluish hues of daylight faded from the late summer sky. Seven minutes later, the rocket was in orbit. Read full article Comments

title: Farmed salmon may not be as nutritious as it once was, new research suggests
raw_text: Eat more fatty fish. That dietary advice has changed the way the world consumes salmon, pushing consumer demand ever upward and production to higher and higher levels. Most of that demand is being met with farmed salmon: Today, nearly 70 percent of the salmon consumed on the planet are raised in pens and cages. The US Department of Agriculture’s Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend eating at least 8 ounces of fish a week and urges people to choose salmon or other species that are similarly high in “heart-healthy” Omega-3 fatty acids. But new research led by USDA scientists finds that levels of these fatty acids in farmed salmon have dropped considerably, potentially making the agency’s own advice, and similar recommendations, including from the American Heart Association, outdated and insufficient. The investigation comes just hours after the electric automaker welcomed hundreds of fans to downtown Austin to ride in the driverless Cybercabs. Tesla plans to deploy the vehicles on its Robotaxi ride-hail network , which is currently operating in a handful of cities in Texas and Florida. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is updating vehicle standards to make it easier and faster for driverless cars to deploy on public roads. It’s currently tweaking eight rules, including those requiring car parts that driverless cars don’t really need: brake pedals, windshield wipers, and rearview mirrors. title: Ask HN: Fable hacked my piano, can I release the results?
raw_text: I have a self playing piano, using a system called PianoDisc Protigy. They have an online store which sells music for their system, from various modern artists along with classics such as Bach and Beethoven. Last night I saw they had released some music from Eric Satre, a 19th century French composer, which I bought. Curious if I could have just used AI to create these files, I began experimenting with Astra and Fable. Feeding the output of one into the other to critique. After an hour of LLM discussion of Rubato and fermata, solenoid response times and proper sustain pedal technique, they settled on their ultimate version of Gymnopedie No 1. I then asked Fable to compare it to the open source version I'd downloaded from Mutopia, which it promptly ripped apart. No sustain, zero rubato, upside down balance. Ok, what about the version I'd just bought? The PianoDisc versions are mp3s encoded with the right channel carrying MIDI to be played on the piano, and the left channel containing any accompanying music to be played through attached speakers (who doesn't want the harmonica on Piano Man?) I gave the mp3 to Fable, which promptly decoded the format, identifying the right channel carrying MIDI using a 2004.5 Hz square wave. It then went on to analyze the nuance of pedal lift and melody relative to the chords. Fable then asked if I wanted it to build an encoder to write my own MIDI files into the right channel of mp3s. title: Limiting Risk in the Face of Uncertainty
raw_text: If you save for retirement when you are young, the standard advice is to emphasize stock-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds. Stocks increase and decrease in dramatic ways that no one can predict reliably, so this approach carries some risk. Fortunately for US stock market investors, that risk has historically been rewarded, on average and over the long term, with high returns. As you approach retirement and need to rely on investments to cover living expenses, the standard advice is to shift your portfolio toward bond-based ETFs or mutual funds. Bonds have had fewer and less dramatic booms and busts. For this reason, they are generally considered less risky than stocks. On average, over the long term, bonds’ safety has meant lower, more reliable returns than stocks. Risk makes less sense for ALA right now. Because of its financial deficit , the Association needs stability. Therefore, in April, ALA’s Endowment Trustees updated the target allocation for the Association’s investment portfolio, reducing our holdings of stocks from 50% to 40%, and increasing ALA’s holdings of bonds from 30% to 40%. As a result, we are sacrificing some projected returns to limit projected risk. If stocks boom as they have in the past few years, ALA’s portfolio will not increase as much as it would have. title: Hoe de VoorleesExpress gezinnen versterkt en bibliotheken scherper laat werken

Al jarenlang werken bibliotheken, vrijwilligers en samenwerkingspartners aan een voorleesritueel bij gezinnen: voor taalplezier, taalontwikkeling én gelijke kansen. Samen bereikten we in Gelderland en Overijssel al meer dan 10.000 gezinnen. Maar door goed te kijken naar wat werkt en wat scherper kan, kunnen we voor méér kinderen en ouders het verschil maken. Hoe voorkom je bijvoorbeeld dat je een deel van de doelgroep mist? En welke gegevens helpen je om de impact zichtbaar te maken? Hiervoor organiseerde Rijnbrink een workshop met het thema ‘Haal meer uit data’, voor VoorleesExpress-projectleiders. In dit artikel vertellen enkele aanwezigen over de waarde van de VoorleesExpress en hoe zij slim gebruikmaken van data. Doe je voordeel met hun ervaringen en tips! Taal begint thuis De kracht van de VoorleesExpress zit in het besef dat taalontwikkeling niet alleen in de klas plaatsvindt. Juist thuis ontstaat de basis. In het contact tussen ouder en kind. In verhalen, gesprekken, rituelen en herhaling. title: Prentenboeken in Papiamentu: een feest van herkenning
raw_text: Een prentenboek vertalen lijkt eenvoudig: je zet de ene taal om in de andere. Maar hoe zorg je ervoor dat een kind zich écht herkent in een verhaal? Voor de nieuwe Papiamentu-prentenboeken – gerealiseerd in het project Leesbevordering in meertalige gezinnen – dachten leden van de klankbordgroep mee over taal, cultuur en geschiedenis. Waarom is de keuze voor opa beter dan de officiële vertaling tawela? Waarom mocht het verhaal van Tula in de nieuwe prentenboekencollectie niet ontbreken? En wat gebeurt er als een kind voor het eerst een verhaal in zijn eigen taal hoort? Jakeema, Myrthe en Margriet vertellen hoe juist die keuzes het verschil maken. Waarom vertalen nodig was Zoals het eerdere artikel over dit project al aangaf: voorlezen stimuleert de taalontwikkeling van jonge kinderen het beste. Juist voorlezen in de thuistaal, de taal van het hart, levert veel extra’s op. Ouders op Bonaire willen dat met alle liefde doen, vertelt Jakeema Hernandez, programmaleider bij Bibliotheek Bonaire. Maar de collectie prentenboeken in het Papiamentu is beperkt. Jakeema is dan ook blij met de nieuwe, vertaalde Papiamentu-boeken. Als kind hield ik al van lezen, maar een boek in mijn eigen taal vinden in de boekhandel of bibliotheek was onmogelijk. Voor mijn inner child is het mooi om te zien dat er nu boeken in het Papiamentu bestaan. title: Bouw je eigen AI-assistent: van losse prompts naar een digitale collega
raw_text: Veel mensen gebruiken AI als vraagbaak: je start een chat, stelt een vraag, krijgt antwoord en begint de volgende keer weer met een nieuwe chat. Een AI-assistent oftewel een ‘custom agent’ werkt net anders: het is een digitale collega die je inwerkt op een specifieke taak. De grootste winst? Die ligt in het automatiseren van repeterende werkzaamheden, zodat er meer tijd overblijft voor strategie, creativiteit en contact met jouw doelgroep. In dit artikel lees je wat een AI-assistent is en hoe je er zelf een kunt inrichten om efficiënter te kunnen werken. Wat is een AI-assistent? Een AI-assistent kun je inrichten om een specifieke taak zo goed mogelijk uit te voeren. In plaats van bij iedere nieuwe chat opnieuw uit te leggen wat je wilt, geef je de assistent vooraf context, instructies en relevante documenten mee. Daardoor begrijpt het programma jouw werkwijze beter en kan het jou consistenter en beter ondersteunen. De AI voert geen autonome taken uit zoals een AI-agent, maar werkt alleen met jouw input. Waar te beginnen? Het kan ingewikkeld klinken, maar om een assistent te kunnen inrichten hoef je geen ICT- of programmeringskennis te hebben. Vrijwel alle AI-platformen bieden de mogelijkheid om een eigen assistent te bouwen. Hierbij is de start het meest belangrijk: een AI-assistent is namelijk zo slim als de informatie waarmee je hem voedt. title: Zó geef je een landelijke campagne een lokale online boost
raw_text: Jaarlijks draaien er meerdere landelijke campagnes waar de bibliotheek aan meedoet, zoals Heel Nederland Leest. Veel mensen kennen de campagne van naam, maar dat betekent niet automatisch een hoge lokale deelname. Door middel van een slimme online campagne kan je hier met relatief weinig extra inspanning verandering in brengen. Je hoeft deze campagne niet vanaf het begin te bouwen, je past alleen de laatste 20 procent aan naar jouw lokale situatie. In dit artikel bespreken we vijf online kansen die de inzet van de offline inzet van jouw bibliotheek een extra boost geven. Landelijke campagnes In dit artikel hebben we het over Heel Nederland Leest, maar onderstaande tips zijn natuurlijk ook toepasbaar op andere landelijke campagnes zoals Kinderboekenweek, Goed Verhaal en de Nationale Voorleesweek. Vertaal de landelijke boodschap naar jouw lokale doelgroep Een voordeel van de landelijke campagne is dat je niet zelf een kernboodschap hoeft te bedenken. Dat is vaak al gedaan en kan je terugvinden in de communicatietoolkit. Dat scheelt weer tijd! Dit jaar is de kernboodschap van Heel Nederland Leest: “Ik doe mee met Heel Nederland Leest. Jij ook?”. Je kunt deze boodschap versterken door in te spelen op jouw lokale situatie en deze op te nemen in je contentstrategie. Om dit goed te kunnen doen heb je een marketingplan en/of contentstrategie nodig. Heb je die nog niet op papier staan?
